questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses **inversion** to emphasise the subject in a conditional clause?
options: If she **hadn’t left**, we would have known about it sooner.
Had she left, we would have known about it sooner.
She left, so we didn’t know about it sooner.
We would have known about it sooner if she left.
questions.answer: Had she left, we would have known about it sooner.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates **cleft sentence construction** with the correct auxiliary verb placement?
options: It was only when I arrived that I realised the mistake.
Only when I arrived did I realise the mistake was obvious.
Realising the mistake was obvious, I arrived late.
The mistake was obvious; I arrived late.
questions.answer: Only when I arrived did I realise the mistake was obvious.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the **subjunctive** to express a hypothetical scenario involving a past event?
options: She wishes she **goes** to the concert tonight.
She wishes she **went** to the concert last night.
She regrets she **didn’t go** to the concert last night.
She hopes she **will go** to the concert tomorrow.
questions.answer: She regrets she **didn’t go** to the concert last night.

questions.question: Which sentence best employs **ellipsis** for conciseness while maintaining grammatical correctness?
options: She said she would call me if she needed anything. She didn’t call, so I assumed she was busy.
She said, ‘Call me if you need anything.’ I didn’t hear back, so I assumed she forgot.
‘Call me if you need anything,’ she said. I didn’t hear from her, so I figured she was avoiding me.
She said she’d call, but she never did, so I took it as a sign she didn’t care.
questions.answer: She said, ‘Call me if you need anything.’ I didn’t hear back, so I assumed she forgot.

questions.question: Which sentence uses **formal register** with the most sophisticated and precise phrasing?
options: The proposal was rejected because it lacked sufficient evidence to support the claims made.
They turned down the idea because it didn’t have enough proof to back up what was said.
The document was dismissed due to insufficient backing for the arguments presented.
The submission was turned down since it didn’t have enough data to make a case.
questions.answer: The proposal was rejected because it lacked sufficient evidence to support the claims made.
